title: Access Studio: choose a route, keep control
idea: Refine the original library-access workbench into a concrete fictional community-event participation journey. Give a patron a visible mission and a small illustrated route board: explore an event, choose what help to seek, inspect an invented registration requirement and decide a next step. All event details and service responses must be clearly authored examples; the interface never registers anybody. Offer a local mock online route, asking staff to explain a step, taking a complete paper route, and pausing or declining. Let choices visibly change the route, help available and unresolved conditions. Introduce a changed condition such as an unfamiliar account requirement or temporarily unavailable staff; the patron can change route without being labeled deficient. Do not ever ask for a password, name, identifier, email, phone or real account information, even in the mock portal. Mock controls should be task choices, not personal-data fields. End in a reviewable, correctable before/after plan describing a chosen route, control boundary, support needed and a fallback. Patron agency and actual service/staff conditions must be coupled: choosing staff help cannot make staff available. Include a second optional fictional situation with fewer suggestions as supported practice, and a complete paper/facilitation packet. The previous library journal is an immutable parent, not an approved service or measured baseline.
domain: Public library digital participation and community service access
people: Adult patrons with varied reading, languages and device access; librarians, volunteers and service owners; none participate in this demonstration.
constraints: No personal information, credentials, account fields, eligibility advice, banking, legal or medical guidance, patron scoring or deficit labels. No real booking, submissions or external links from the generated candidate. No network, storage, telemetry or external assets. Main path must use concrete route choices, authored consequences and at most two optional open-text fields; never solicit personal detail. Plain language, visual hierarchy with text alternatives, responsive layout, keyboard/focus support, cancel and faithful correction, cover/resume and confirmed complete clearing for shared-device handoff. Put detailed review metadata in Help. Passing, oral assistance, paper and stopping are legitimate choices; do not promise available staff, connectivity, translation or service capacity. Provide complete invented paper materials, not a sentence suggesting paper. The design brief must map relevant roles and proposed task lenses to product requirements, rationale, interactions, acceptance checks and evidence boundaries. Patron/librarian/practitioner review, accessibility/usability, field pilot, learning, transfer and flourishing remain untested. Source preferably below 60000 bytes in file-writing delivery; develop a distinct access journey rather than the school-science interaction.
